jobs.occupation: Engineer, New Technology & Innovation - Acoustic Measurement & Evaluation
jobs.description:
Do you want to work for some of the world’s leading audio brands? Become a part of the HARMAN team and get to work for JBL and Harman/Kardon.

By joining HARMAN, you'll dive headfirst into the exciting world of headphones, portable speakers, party boxes and other audio technologies, and contribute to the success of Harman Lifestyle EMEA business. The consumer audio industry is fast paced, fun and dynamic and we’re looking for someone who is proactive, loves to work with a lot of different stakeholders from all over Europe and has creative ideas.

You will join our new Acoustics Engineering Lab within Harman Consumer Audio, based in Kvistgaard, Denmark in the position of:

Engineer New Technology & Innovation - Acoustic Measurement & Evaluation

Introduction: A Career at HARMAN Lifestyle:

We’re a global, multi-disciplinary team that’s putting the innovative power of technology to work and transforming tomorrow. As a member of HARMAN Lifestyle, you connect consumers with the power of superior sound.

• Contribute your talents to high-end, esteemed brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, Mark Levinson and Revel.

• Unite your passion for audio innovation with high-tech product development.

• Create pitch-perfect, cutting-edge technology that elevates listening experience.

HARMAN’s engineers and designers are creative, purposeful and agile. As part of this team, you’ll combine your technical expertise with innovative ideas to help drive cutting-edge solutions in the consumer audio systems. Every day, you will push the boundaries of creative design, and HARMAN is committed to providing you with the opportunities, innovative technologies and resources to build a successful career.

What You’ll Be Part Of

The Consumer Audio New Technology & Innovation (NT&I) team is at the center of audio technology innovation, supporting the development of HARMAN's next-generation consumer audio products, including over-ear headphones, true wireless stereo (TWS) earbuds, and open wireless stereo (OWS) devices. The NT&I Denmark team is seeking a Senior Engineer, Acoustic Measurement & Evaluation, to lead the development, execution, and continuous improvement of acoustic measurement and subjective evaluation methodologies for consumer audio products.

The successful candidate will be responsible for objective acoustic characterization of loudspeakers, headphones, earbuds, and emerging audio devices, as well as the design and management of laboratory test environments and listening evaluation programs.

This role combines deep expertise in electroacoustic measurements, data analysis, listening science, and laboratory operations to ensure industry-leading audio performance across our product portfolio.

How You’ll Make An Impact:

• Technical Leadership: Provide technical leadership in acoustic measurement and evaluation, establishing best practices, and driving continuous improvement of measurement capabilities, tools, and processes.

• Acoustic Measurement & Characterization: Lead the objective acoustic characterization of speakers, headphones, earbuds, and emerging audio products, utilizing advanced measurement techniques to assess frequency response, distortion, directivity, sensitivity, noise performance, and sound pressure capabilities.

• Subjective Evaluation & Listening Science: Design and conduct subjective listening evaluations, including listener panel management, competitive benchmarking, and the development of scientifically robust methodologies for assessing sound quality and user experience.

• Data Analysis & Performance Insights: Analyse and interpret objective and subjective performance data, generating actionable insights and developing meaningful correlations between acoustic measurements and listener preferences.

• Measurement Methodology & Standards: Develop, validate, and maintain measurement methodologies and standards, ensuring acoustic evaluations are accurate, repeatable, and aligned across development teams and laboratories.

• Acoustic Laboratory Development: Design, establish, and maintain state-of-the-art acoustic test facilities, including listening rooms, anechoic and semi-anechoic environments, ear-simulator and HATS-based measurement systems, and automated test platforms.

• Collaboration: Provide acoustic measurement and evaluation support for internally developed technologies, algorithms, and proof-of-concept systems, and collaborate with cross-functional teams on product validation, troubleshooting, performance optimization, and deployment.

What Makes You A Strong Fit:

Education & Experience:

• M.S. or Ph.D. in Acoustics, Audio Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Physics, or a related field.

• At least 8 years of experience in acoustic measurement, audio product development, electroacoustic testing, or acoustic research.

• Demonstrated experience leading technical initiatives and driving improvements in measurement methodologies, laboratory capabilities, or audio evaluation processes.

Technical Skills:

• Strong expertise in objective acoustic measurement and characterization of speakers, headphones, earbuds, and related audio systems, including frequency response, distortion, directivity, sensitivity, noise, and SPL performance.

• Deep understanding of psychoacoustics, listening science, and subjective evaluation methodologies (e.g., MUSHRA test) including statistical analysis.

• Hands-on experience with industry-standard tools such as Audio Precision APx, SoundCheck, ear simulators, and precision measurement microphones (e.g., from Brüel & Kjær, GRAS).

• Proficiency in Python and/or MATLAB for measurement automation, signal processing, data analysis, and visualization.

Bonus Points if You Have:

• Experience with active noise control, headphone hear-through, spatial audio, noise reduction, AI-based audio processing, and other advanced audio technologies.

• Experience applying AI and data-driven approaches to acoustic evaluation, listening-test analysis, perceptual modelling, or measurement automation.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively within and across teams.

• Self-motivated, proactive, and capable of driving projects with a high degree of ownership.

• Passion for audio quality, innovation, and continuous learning.

Things To Know:

• This position collaborates with global teams, and occasional early-morning or evening meetings may be required to work with colleagues in China and the United States.

• Occasional international travel to other HARMAN sites is required.

• Professional working proficiency in English is required for effective day-to-day communication with regional engineering teams.

• Successfully complete a background investigation and drug screen as a condition of employment (post-offer).

What You Can Expect:

• A hybrid work environment that balances flexibility with in-person collaboration, with most office-based roles onsite three days a week.

• Access to employee discounts on HARMAN and Samsung products (including JBL, Harman / Kardon, AKG, and others).

• Learning and development opportunities through our award-winning HARMAN University programs.

• Wellness benefits designed to support your overall well-being.

• Tuition reimbursement support.

• Access to the HARMAN campus fitness center and cafeteria, where available.

• An inclusive and diverse work environment that supports both your professional and personal development.

jobs.occupation: Sales Manager, Equipment Sales
jobs.description:
Sales Manager, Equipment Sales

Are you a tenacious and commercially driven sales professional with experience in the space industry? Do you enjoy working directly with customers, taking ownership of sales opportunities and turning them into business?

We are looking for a hands-on Sales Manager to join our Equipment Sales team. You will take responsibility for driving sales opportunities forward from initial customer engagement to order placement.

Working closely with the Director of Equipment Sales and the wider team, you will contribute directly to our commercial success through customer engagement, key account management and consistent execution of sales activities.

You are proactive in assessing opportunities, identifying the most valuable next steps and contributing to the team's commercial priorities. You take initiative, communicate openly and work collaboratively to ensure that efforts are aligned and directed towards the team's overall objectives.

This is a role for someone who combines commercial drive with a structured and pragmatic approach, and who takes pride in following through on commitments and delivering tangible results.

You can be based at our headquarters in Aalborg, Denmark or our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Your Responsibilities

• Execute sales opportunities from initial customer enquiry or engagement through qualification, proposals, negotiations and order placement, taking ownership of the sales process and customer dialogue throughout.

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective customers, with a particular focus on key account management and converting customer opportunities into business.

• Assess sales opportunities, identify commercial potential and recommend priorities and next steps in close dialogue with the Director of Equipment Sales and the wider team. Take ownership of executing agreed priorities and maintaining progress.

• Manage all sales administration related to your opportunities, including CRM updates, pipeline management, quotations, commercial proposals, customer correspondence, contracts, order documentation, reporting and forecasting.

• Coordinate relevant technical and commercial input from colleagues, ensuring professional and timely customer responses and proposals, while working in accordance with established sales processes and the team's ways of working.

• Contribute to the team's commercial objectives through consistent sales execution and achievement of your individual revenue target. Represent Space Inventor at international conferences and customer meetings, developing relationships and identifying relevant commercial opportunities.

Qualifications

• Proven sales experience within the space domain is a requirement, with a demonstrated ability to convert sales opportunities into business and achieve revenue targets.

• Experience with equipment or technically complex products is an advantage, as are strong customer relationship and key account management skills.

• Tenacious and persistent, with the determination to follow through, maintain momentum and bring sales opportunities to a conclusion.

• Structured and disciplined, with the ability to manage multiple sales opportunities and ensure that commitments, follow-ups and sales administration are handled reliably.

• Pragmatic and solution-oriented, with a focus on delivering results and creating value through established processes and ways of working.

• Able to work independently, take initiative and collaborate effectively with colleagues, ensuring that individual sales activities contribute to the team's shared commercial objectives.

• Willing and able to travel internationally approximately 20–30 days per year for conferences and customer visits.

What We Offer

• A full-time role with exposure to a variety of disciplines within space technology.

• A position in an exciting, rapidly growing industry with significant international reach.

• A chance to shape your role and responsibilities within a growing company.

• Great colleagues and several social events each year.

• Health insurance and additional employee benefits.

• Competitive salary and good working conditions.

How to Apply

If you’re ready to take your career to the next level, apply by submitting your CV and application. If you have any questions about the position, feel free to contact us via jobs@space-inventor.com, and we’ll get back to you as soon as possible.

Interviews are held continuously until the right candidate is found.

Start date to be agreed, but preferably with start-up as soon as possible.

We look forward to receiving your application.

About Space Inventor

Space Inventor is a leading Satellite company with a passion and drive for exploring space and delivering innovative solutions in satellite technology. Our mission is to revolutionize the space industry with creativity, technical expertise, and reliability. With our 250+ years of combined experience in the space industry, we are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what satellites can achieve.

Are you good at creating an overview, keeping operations running smoothly, and motivating the people around you? Your responsibilities will include:

jobs.occupation: Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. As the most senior engineer on the team, you will own the technical direction of the platform security, identity, and network security slice, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across platform security, identity, and network security, and rolling out the first paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, CVE response, CI/CD identity, and a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen). You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers write, review and ship secure systems.

**What You Will Do

**You will join a focused platform security team and operate as its most senior engineer. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities, and we expect this role to set the bar.

• Design and build the paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, and CVE response, running inside the pipelines teams already use, with findings routed to the owners who can fix them under tracked SLAs

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for a unified internal network and VPN across GCP, AWS, and our Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen offices, while the team that owns the network keeps running it

• Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own

• Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves

• Build audit logging as a shared capability that teams plug into rather than reinvent

• Turn GRC controls into technical implementations, with evidence pipelines that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Own the contracting cycle for external penetration tests and build the intake, classification, and tracking system that routes findings to named owners, while the owning teams remediate

• Hand each capability off cleanly, with a runbook, a named owner, and an escalation path, and run office hours where product and platform teams can get a security review or a paved-road question answered

• Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

**What You Could Bring

**This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

• Platform security: you have run vulnerability scanning, CVE management, and image scanning at scale, and you know the operational reality of getting CVEs fixed, beyond standing up the tooling

• Identity and auth: you have worked hands-on inside an auth codebase, rolled out MFA on live systems, and managed token lifecycles in CI/CD with OIDC and workload identity

• Network security at scale: you have designed and run a unified internal network across multiple cloud providers and offices, with a VPN approach that holds up

• Platform-as-product mindset: you have built internal security tooling that other teams chose to adopt, with guard rails built into the tools developers already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured the impact

• Infrastructure as Code: strong experience with Terraform, Crossplane, or similar

Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. This role sets the technical direction for the team's quarterly missions. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on three or four items but not all of them, apply anyway. The "deep in one, ready to grow into the other" framing above is not a hedge, it is how we actually hire at this level. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

jobs.occupation: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
**About The Role

**We sell electricity data through an API: carbon intensity, power prices and grid forecasts. Tech companies use it to report and minimize emissions. Wind and solar producers and grid-scale battery solutions use it to predict prices and plan their market participation. EV companies use it to build smart-charging features. CS is about ensuring every one of these customers actually uses the data to do their job better, stays with us and grows with us.

You’ll build out Customer Success at Electricity Maps. That means onboarding new customers, running renewals and spotting where an account could grow, while trialling and defining the processes and tooling that make it all repeatable. There’s a basic CS setup in place, but the playbook is yours to write. You’ll play a critical role in how CS evolves at Electricity Maps, and in our company’s success.

You'll work closely with Sales, Product and our Data team. This is a hands-on role: you'll own your own book of customers and a retention target.

**What You'll Do

**

• Own the end-to-end customer journey. Onboarding, product value, retention, expansion. Your job is to make sure our data delivers real value to each customer, and you’ll be measured on their retention and growth (Net Revenue Retention).

• Get new customers to value fast. Take the handoff from Sales, set expectations, and help customers get set up using the API. Find ways to hone our customer onboarding to create a smoother, better process.

• Own renewals and growth. Run renewal processes end-to-end, from positioning and proposal through signature. Proactively identify and close expansion: new zones, new data types or use cases, other teams in the same company.

• Go beyond the technical contact. Build relationships across each customer’s organization, branching out past technical contacts to understand and align with the business outcomes the data supports. Build executive relationships with strategic accounts, and run periodic business reviews that tie our data to their goals.

• Manage a mixed book. Your accounts will range from high-profile logos to smaller customers, with deal sizes to match. You’ll juggle competing priorities, keep an eye on the details, and find the right way to serve each account, so every customer gets real value and results for them and for Electricity Maps.

• Build the low-touch motion. Design the onboarding, check-in and renewal sequences that serve the long tail of customers who are smaller value and have less growth potential. In short, you’ll help us learn how best we can serve these customers at scale.

• Connect customers and product. Find out what customers are building, where they get stuck and what we could do better. Identify themes, and relay insights internally to help shape Product and Sales strategies. In return also keep customers close to our roadmap: new zones, forecast model improvements, and what’s coming.

• Build the tools you need. The tooling behind CS is yours to shape. Where there’s a gap, from health scoring and renewal alerts to onboarding flows and automated emails, you’ll build the solution yourself instead of waiting for someone else to.

**What We're Looking For

****Must-haves

jobs.occupation: DevOps / Platform Engineer — Reliability, Performance & Production Ownership
jobs.description:
DevOps / Platform Engineer — Fully Remote, Performance & Production Ownership

Want to work fully remotely with real freedom and ownership while operating high-throughput, low-latency systems that serve billions of shoppers?

For the right person, this is a high-trust role where you have flexibility in how you structure your work and the opportunity to make a significant impact on the technology behind billions of e-commerce experiences.

We’re building the infrastructure behind better e-commerce experiences for billions of shoppers every year.

Our systems serve more than 2,000 requests per second. Our in-house search engine delivers a p50 latency of sub-ms, while our entire infrastructure maintains 99.998% uptime.

We work with modern technology, use AI as a fundamental part of how we build, and continuously push the limits of reliability, performance, and innovation. Our goal is simple: connect e-commerce shoppers with the right products at the right time while helping merchants create a better customer experience and improve their bottom line.

We’re proud of the systems we’ve built—and we want someone who is excited to help make them even faster, more reliable, and more capable.

This job will be perfect for you if

• You enjoy operating high-throughput production systems where latency, reliability, and customer impact matter

• You care deeply about reliability, latency, throughput, and system performance

• You can investigate problems across infrastructure, application code, databases, queues, and networks

• You are comfortable reading, writing, debugging, and optimising production code

• You proactively identify failure scenarios before they become incidents

• You build automation and tooling instead of accepting repetitive manual work

• You enjoy improving CI/CD, infrastructure as code, observability, and developer experience

• You have handled serious production incidents and understand the responsibility that comes with on-call

• You think beyond whether a deployment succeeded and care about how the system behaves afterwards

• You can communicate clearly during incidents and take ownership when things matter

• You are curious about new technology and enjoy finding better ways to build and operate systems

• You want to work closely with software engineers rather than treating infrastructure as a separate world

• You thrive in a remote environment where freedom is matched by responsibility

A normal day for you

No two days will be the same, but your work might include:

• Investigating why a service, query, or piece of application code is slower than it should be

• Improving the reliability and performance of systems serving thousands of requests per second

• Reviewing metrics, traces, logs, and alerts to identify issues before they affect customers

• Designing and implementing infrastructure, automation, and internal tooling

• Writing, reviewing, debugging, and optimising production code

• Working with developers to improve how systems are built, deployed, and operated

• Responding to incidents when needed, then making sure the underlying problem is permanently addressed

• Exploring how new technologies and AI-powered tools can improve our engineering workflow

• Thinking proactively about scaling, capacity, resilience, and potential failure scenarios

AI is part of the job

We’re an AI-first company. AI and agentic coding are already part of how we build, investigate, automate, and improve systems.

You should already be comfortable using AI in your daily engineering workflow—for example, to investigate incidents, generate and review code, build internal tooling, automate operational work, and improve your own productivity.

How we work

This role can be fully remote for the right person.

We believe in giving people the freedom to structure their work in a way that helps them perform at their best. We care about impact, ownership, communication, and results—not about watching when or where you work.

You’ll need to work with meaningful overlap during CET working hours and participate in our PagerDuty/on-call rotation. Freedom comes with responsibility, especially when you are responsible for production systems.

On-call includes holidays

If you are scheduled to be on call and a genuine production alarm goes off—whether that is on a normal weekday, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Eve, or New Year’s Day—you are expected to respond, take ownership, and stay with the issue until our systems are fully up and running again.

This is an important part of the role and is not optional. We are looking for someone who genuinely stands behind their work and understands that production ownership sometimes means being there when things go wrong.

At the same time, your goal is to make this situation as rare as possible. The best engineer is not the person who enjoys firefighting every holiday, but the person who builds reliable systems, strong monitoring, and effective automation so that firefighting is never needed.

How to apply

Instead of starting with a traditional cover letter, please send us a maximum 10-minute video.

We are hiring a human being—not AI-generated slop, a spotless resume, or someone who simply knows how to present the right keywords. We know the kind of person we are looking for, but the process also needs to be mutual. You should get the opportunity to meet the people behind the company and decide whether this is the right environment for you.

That is why we want to meet you upfront and see how you think, communicate, and explain your experience—not only evaluate what is written on paper.

**In The Video, Please Tell Us

**

• Who you are

• The production systems you have owned

• A difficult reliability or performance problem you solved

• What you changed and the measurable result

• How you approach incidents and on-call responsibility

• How you currently use AI and agentic coding

• Why you believe you would be a strong fit for this role

• What you are looking for in your next team and role

The video does not need to be polished. Please don’t spend time producing a perfect presentation or reading a script. We want to see the real person, understand how you think, and hear about the work you have actually done.

You may also include a short written example of a system that was slow, unreliable, or difficult to operate. Explain how you found the root cause, what you changed, and what improved afterwards.

If you are primarily an infrastructure administrator, this probably isn’t the right role. If you are a production-minded software engineer who enjoys making systems faster, more reliable, and easier to operate, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.description:

At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, Department of Chemistry and Bioscience, a Ph.D. stipend is available within the general study program. **The work of the PhD candidate is multifaceted. The candidate will develop on a metagenomic assay to enable the detection of RNA viruses from cell-free nucleic acid material from plasma samples. Furthermore, we will build a reference database of genomes for selected pathogens isolated from neonates and use this – in collaboration with project-associated physicians – to understand if genomic signatures can be used to predict clinical outcomes. Finally, we will analyse plasma samples from a prospective cohort of neonates with sepsis – inclusion has passed 200 neonates already – to determine the feasibility of using metagenomics in this patient indication based on comparison to state-of-the-art microbiological methods.

The work will be carried out in an interdisciplinary research group of neonatal physicians, clinical microbiologists, molecular biologists, and bioinformaticians.

jobs.occupation: Growth Analyst
jobs.description:
_Hybrid, Copenhagen based - report to SVP Growth

_**About The Role

**OrderYOYO builds the ordering apps and websites that thousands of restaurants across seven European markets use to take orders directly from their own customers. Our Growth team has one number to move: average orders per day per restaurant partner.

We're looking for a Growth Data Analyst to find where those orders are being lost, design the experiments that win them back, and prove it with data — across the end-user apps (iOS and Android), the restaurant partner websites, and the marketing stack.

This is a hands-on role. You'll write the SQL, build the test, read the result, and present it to the people who decide what ships next — working alongside a developer, a marketing manager, a paid media manager, and a data engineer.

**Role Mission

**Grow average orders per day per restaurant partner by finding where orders are lost across apps, websites and marketing channels, running the experiments that win them back, and making the Growth numbers trustworthy enough to decide on.

**Core Responsibilities

**

• Own the end-user funnel view — from visit to order to repeat order — across apps and RP websites, by country and by restaurant partner.

• Run cohort, funnel, and retention analyses to find the biggest leaks in traffic, conversion, and repeat ordering, and size what fixing each one is worth in orders per day.

• Turn findings into a ranked backlog of hypotheses with expected impact and effort, and defend the ranking with the Growth team and Product.

• Design A/B tests end to end — hypothesis, success metric, guardrails, sample size and runtime, randomisation unit, and a pre-registered analysis plan — and set them up yourself on the apps and RP websites, working with the developer on feature flags or variant logic where code changes are needed.

• Check tests while they run (sample ratio, instrumentation, novelty effects) and read them out honestly, including when the result is flat or negative.

• Bring the same discipline to the marketing stack — paid media (Google Ads, Meta), email and push, SMS, landing pages, and restaurant partners' Google Business Profiles — using geo or restaurant-level splits and holdouts where a user-level test isn't possible, and judging traffic quality and incrementality on orders, not clicks.

• Own the definitions of the Growth metrics (AOD, conversion rate, new vs returning, retention), keep them consistent between GA4, the apps, and the warehouse, and chase tracking gaps with the data engineer and developer until fixes are verified with data.

• Partner with Algirdas on the Growth dashboards in Fabric and Power BI so reporting is automated rather than produced by hand.

• Build and own the experimentation playbook, and use AI as a daily tool — for SQL, analysis plans, and readouts — helping the team build small, repeatable AI workflows such as pre-test power calculations or weekly funnel checks. Experimentation is too important to be guesswork.

**Must-Have Requirements

**

• 3 to 5 years in product, growth, or marketing analytics, ideally in a consumer app, marketplace, e-commerce, or food ordering business.

• Strong SQL — able to write and debug multi-step queries over event and transaction data without help.

• A track record of designing, running, and reading A/B tests, with the statistics to do it properly: power and sample size, significance, guardrail metrics, and the common ways a test lies (peeking, sample ratio mismatch, novelty).

• Technical enough to set up a test yourself: comfortable with feature flags or an experimentation tool, basic JavaScript or app event instrumentation, and reading a tracking plan.

• Hands-on with a product or web analytics stack (GA4 or similar) and a BI tool (Power BI, Looker, Tableau, or similar).

• Comfortable testing in marketing channels as well as in product: campaign experiments in Google Ads or Meta, email or push tests, and geo or holdout designs for measuring incrementality.

• Uses AI tools daily for analysis work and can show how it changed the way you work.

• Clear, confident communication — able to take a messy result and explain to a non-technical audience what it means and what to do next, in writing and in person.

• Owns outcomes, not tasks, and is comfortable setting the plan in a small team rather than waiting for one.

• Fluent English. Danish is not required.

**Strong-to-Have Experience

**

• Python or R for statistical analysis and automating recurring checks.

• Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, or another lakehouse and BI setup.

• Mobile app experimentation (Firebase, Optimizely, GrowthBook, Statsig, or similar) and web experimentation on multi-tenant or white-label sites.

• Sequential or Bayesian test methods, or quasi-experiments where a true A/B test isn't possible (for example, market-level or restaurant-level rollouts).

• Paid media data (Google Ads, Meta) and attribution, to judge traffic quality as well as conversion.

• A customer data platform and B2C engagement tooling (Segment, Braze, Firebase messaging, or similar), including running lifecycle tests in them.

• Building AI-assisted workflows or agents for analysis, not only using chat tools.

**Who We Are

**At OrderYOYO, company culture comes first. We create a positive, inclusive environment where people are trusted to do their best work and take ownership of what they build. Personal development is central to how we work — engineers are encouraged to grow technically, take responsibility, and help shape how our products and platforms evolve.

We help restaurants succeed online by providing branded websites, mobile apps, and tailored marketing solutions, giving them full control of their business. By removing high commission fees charged by third-party platforms, we empower restaurants to grow sustainably.

Through our partnership with AppSmart, the market leader in POS and in-store systems, we've become the largest restaurant-focused platform in Europe.

**What We Offer

**

• A salary of DKK59,000/ month

• A hybrid role based in Copenhagen.

• High ownership and autonomy over the analysis and experiments you run.

• The opportunity to directly move a revenue-critical metric: orders per day.

• A strong focus on data quality, honest experimentation, and analytics best practices.

• A collaborative, international Growth team.

• Real emphasis on learning, mentoring, and personal development.
